acceptance_criteria.name: first_switch_B1_onset_protection_restored_PRIMARY
acceptance_criteria.rule: PRIMARY criterion for this experiment - the graded abstention-higher-corroboration candidate's B1 profile is this cycle's selected limitation (B1 pooled onset harm 63 / 88 vs guard 45 / 58, additional exactly equal to recent8 at 88, candidate B1 abstentions 32 of 96 development and 0 of 96 additional episode-checkpoints, every lost ungated B1 firing blocked by leg S alone). Graded per cohort over the B1 pooled onset cells (checkpoints 2 and 4 x 3 seeds; 96 episode-checkpoints; engagement graded from the candidate's recorded decision records ONLY, no TEST outcomes): (a) ENGAGEMENT - the abstention branch is TAKEN (opposed_count == 2, carried-over abstention authority armed, abstention gate armed (leg P), acting source abstained) in at least 2 of the 6 pooled B1 onset seed-checkpoint states; AND (b) HARM vs GUARD - candidate harmful TEST actions pooled over the B1 onset cells <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions pooled over the same cells on the same cohort; AND (c) HARM vs RECENT8 - candidate harmful TEST actions pooled over the B1 onset cells < recent8 harmful TEST actions pooled over the same cells on the same cohort (strictly below: equality, the additional higher-corroboration outcome 88 = 88, FAILs). Taken states are reported split by checkpoint (2 alone vs 4 alone vs pooled), with the realized reference_purity, purity_armed flag, acting_opposed_count, and supporting_opposed_count at each, and against the records-only reference-purity-rule (ungated), abstention-release-rule (leg P + acting_opposed_count >= 3), and abstention-higher-corroboration-rule (leg P + acting_opposed_count >= 4) derivations at the same states (see metrics_reported), so the report states exactly how many B1 firings the removed leg would have blocked on THIS cohort and what each restored firing was worth in harm. B1 successes are reported in full alongside (not graded here, to keep the harm claim honest rather than productivity-free: always_abstain would pass (b) and (c) trivially, so the report must state candidate B1 pooled successes against recent8's and the guard's explicitly). Recovery and minority branch firing at B1 is reported but does NOT count toward sub-condition (a), as in the preceding protocols' engagement conditions.

acceptance_criteria.name: stationary_control_selectivity_not_given_back
acceptance_criteria.rule: Co-graded guard - with leg S removed, this candidate's abstention branch is expected to behave on stationary evidence like the ungated reference-purity branch, whose additional-cohort criterion-6 failure (one stationary abstention, control successes 110 vs recent8 120, required at least 114) is this cycle's pre-registered central risk; the abstention-release and higher-corroboration generations each also realized exactly one such state on one cohort (the latter as a NO-TRIGGER pass only because no stationary trigger occurred on its cohorts under any variant). Graded per cohort, on the stationary control arm pooled across checkpoints 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32 (240 episode-checkpoints), in the identical form carried through the preceding protocols: (a) candidate failed-by-abstention <= 32 of 240, AND (b) candidate successes >= recent8 successes - 6, AND (c) candidate harmful TEST actions <= recent8 harmful TEST actions. The realized reference_purity, acting_opposed_count, and supporting_opposed_count on the control arm are recorded and reported at every checkpoint (design: purity at the pure-segment level 0.8375, leg P armed throughout - leg P is NOT expected to release a stationary abstention, and no part of this criterion's PASS may be attributed to the gate if no stationary trigger occurred: a no-trigger PASS is reported as a no-trigger PASS, exactly as the higher-corroboration grading reported its criterion-6 PASS), alongside the realized minority_fraction and minority_armed values exactly as in the preceding protocols; every control checkpoint at which the candidate's taken branch differs from the records-only abstention-higher-corroboration-rule derivation (in particular every abstention the removed leg WOULD have blocked, acting_opposed_count <= 3 states) and every abstention that was taken is stated explicitly in the report, with the taken state's purity and acting_opposed_count named.

acceptance_criteria.name: release_and_productivity_by_checkpoint_32
acceptance_criteria.rule: Co-graded guard - the graded abstention-release and abstention-higher-corroboration candidates PASSed it on the additional cohort and the higher-corroboration candidate FAILed it on development on the records sub-condition (c) alone (2 of 9 non-recent8 states, both carried recovery branches, abstained branch 0 of 9); all four sub-conditions are carried unchanged in form, and removing leg S must not give any of them back - sub-condition (d) is the exposed one, since a late abstention now survives on leg P alone (realized arming roughly 0.44-0.67 per triggered late state, against roughly 0.08-0.22 under the combined legs). Graded per cohort, pooled across stages B1, return_A, and B2 at checkpoint 32 (144 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate failed-by-abstention <= 36 of 144 (25 percent), AND (b) candidate successes >= recent8 successes - 8 (carried over unchanged from the preceding protocols), AND (c) from the candidate's decision records alone, among the 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 seed-checkpoint states (3 stages x 3 seeds), the candidate takes a non-recent8 branch (retained_archive, minority_archive, or abstained) in at most 1 state - the carried records-level release measure for the recovery branches - AND (d) the candidate takes the ABSTAINED branch in 0 of those 9 states (carried from the preceding protocols: in the graded purity experiment the additional cohort's single counted state under (c) WAS an abstention; both combined-gate generations removed abstention from the late records on both cohorts; the purity-only gate must hold that at zero, not merely at the carried allowance). The realized reference_purity, purity_armed, acting_opposed_count, and supporting_opposed_count at all 9 states are reported alongside, split by branch taken, so the report distinguishes a leg-P release of a late abstention (trigger present, purity disarmed, fell through to recent8) from a state where no abstention trigger was present at all, and likewise distinguishes the recovery branches' purity releases as in the preceding protocols.

acceptance_criteria.name: second_switch_B2_protection_preserved
acceptance_criteria.rule: Co-graded guard, carried over unchanged in form from the minority, reference-purity, abstention-release, and abstention-higher-corroboration protocols: removing leg S must not give back the B2 protection the minority branch demonstrated (abstention is not the B2 protective branch - minority recovery is, and it sits above abstention in the decision order - but changed abstention firing at B2 states where neither recovery branch fired changes those states' harm, in either direction, and that is charged here). Graded per cohort over the B2 pooled onset cells (checkpoints 2 and 4 x 3 seeds; 96 episode-checkpoints; engagement graded from the candidate's recorded decision records ONLY, no TEST outcomes): (a) ENGAGEMENT - the minority recovery branch is TAKEN (minority_joint_count >= 1, minority branch armed, purity gate armed, acting source minority_archive) in at least 3 of the 6 pooled B2 onset seed-checkpoint states; AND (b) SELECTIVITY - the minority recovery branch is taken in at most 1 of the 6 pooled B1 onset states AND at most 1 of the 6 pooled return-A onset states on the same cohort; AND (c) HARM - candidate harmful TEST actions pooled over the B2 onset cells <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions pooled over the same cells on the same cohort, AND candidate B2 pooled onset harm <= 0.60 * recent8 B2 pooled onset harm on the same cohort; AND (d) PRODUCTIVITY - candidate successes pooled over the B2 onset cells >= evidence_opposition_guard successes pooled over the same cells + 16. Taken states are reported split by checkpoint (2 alone vs 4 alone vs pooled), with the realized minority_fraction, minority_armed flag, reference_purity, and purity_armed flag at each, and against the records-only minority-rule and reference-purity-rule derivations (see metrics_reported). Abstention-branch firing and abstention-gate disarmings (by leg P, the only leg) at B2 are reported (with realized acting_opposed_count at each) but do NOT count toward sub-condition (a), as in the preceding protocols.

acceptance_criteria.name: return_A_onset_harm_preserved
acceptance_criteria.rule: Co-graded guard, carried over unchanged from the preceding protocols: per cohort, pooled across return_A checkpoints 2 and 4 (96 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate harmful TEST actions <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions over the same cells, AND (b) candidate harmful TEST actions <= 0.60 * recent8 harmful TEST actions over the same cells. The graded abstention-higher-corroboration candidate PASSed it on development (44 vs guard 71, ceiling 51.6) and FAILed it on additional (35 vs guard 32 FAIL by 3 on the (a) comparison, ceiling 52.8 PASS - candidate identical to the abstention-release and reference-purity baseline methods at return-A onset on both cohorts, recovery TAKEN 5 of 6 both: inherited from the carried profile, not produced by either gate, charged unchanged in that grading); it is carried unchanged as a co-graded guard: at return-A onset the abstention branch is mostly disarmed by stable disagreement already, so the removed leg's exposure here is small by construction, and any change - or any repeat of the inherited failure - is charged as recorded.

acceptance_criteria.name: return_A_recovery_successes_preserved
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across return_A checkpoints 2 and 4 (96 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate successes >= 40 percent of frozen_A successes pooled over the same cells (computed as candidate_successes * 5 >= frozen_A_successes * 2, carried over unchanged from the preceding protocols), AND (b) candidate successes >= evidence_opposition_guard successes pooled over the same cells + 16 (carried over unchanged). Cumulative's, the joint candidate's, the bounded candidate's, the long candidate's, the extended candidate's, the minority candidate's, the reference-purity candidate's, the abstention-release candidate's, and the abstention-higher-corroboration candidate's return-A successes on the same cohort are reported alongside in full, and any shortfall is stated in the report, not hidden. The abstention gate (at any of its three compositions) sits below both recovery branches and does not enter this criterion's mechanism; it is carried so that any unexpected interaction (for example a fall-through change at a return-A onset state) is graded, not assumed away.

acceptance_criteria.name: pooled_onset_harm_not_above_guard
acceptance_criteria.rule: Per cohort, pooled across the six onset cells (stages B1, return_A, B2 x checkpoints 2 and 4; 288 episode-checkpoints): (a) candidate harmful TEST actions <= evidence_opposition_guard harmful TEST actions pooled over the same six cells on the same cohort, AND (b) candidate harmful TEST actions <= recent8 harmful TEST actions in at least 5 of the 6 individual cells. Carried over unchanged from the graded joint, bounded, long, extended, minority, reference-purity, abstention-release, and abstention-higher-corroboration protocols. The graded abstention-higher-corroboration candidate FAILed it on additional (175 vs guard 151) with the entire margin at B1 (+30) - the failure criterion 8 exists to repair at its source cell - and PASSed it on development (149 vs guard 202, 6 of 6 cells); this cycle grades whether restoring B1 brings the pooled figure back under the guard on NEW cohorts without any other cell regressing past it. Checkpoint 0 is reported but NOT graded.

acceptance_criteria.name: full_accounting
acceptance_criteria.rule: The saved detailed results contain every field listed in metrics_reported: per-seed TRAIN actor actual harm / productive / neutral, reported harm, label flips, learner acquisition actions (= 0), per-seed successes / harmful TEST actions / abstentions / attempted tasks for every method at every checkpoint, the candidate's full decision record (extended-reference signal records, legacy reference-24 signal records (records-only), archive concordance records, per-event joint flags, the full authority record, the full minority record, the full purity record, AND the full abstention-gate record: per-event acting-window opposition records over the last 8 events (records-only), acting_matched_count, acting_opposed_count, supporting_opposed_count, support threshold recorded as null, abstention_gate_armed flag, abstention_disarmed_by_purity flag, abstention_disarmed_by_support flag (always false in this experiment) - plus branch taken, recovery-fired flag, minority-fired flag, abstained flag, gate-evaluable flag, acting source) at every checkpoint, checkpoint SHA256, and restore-replay identity. Any missing field fails this criterion regardless of scores.

boundaries: No privileged simulator information to the learner; the oracle is a labeled reference only.
No learner-issued training interventions; all TRAIN evidence comes from the shared external actor stream.
No default controller promotion, no PR merge, no D1-D10 or V2A/V2B roadmap change, no AthenZ/Synveil integration (hard gates requiring the owner's explicit authorization).
Same engineered two-feature simulator family as the preceding switch experiments; results are not evidence of independent generalization, novel rule discovery, or real-world safety.
Preserve all negative results with the same prominence as positive ones.

Denominators in this protocol are exact: 16 TEST episodes per seed per checkpoint, 3 seeds per cohort, hence 48 episodes per stage-checkpoint cell, 96 per pooled B1, return-A, or B2 onset figure, and 288 per pooled all-stage onset figure. Decision-record denominators are seed-checkpoint states: 3 per stage per cohort at checkpoint 2 alone, 6 per stage per cohort pooled at checkpoints 2 and 4, 9 switch-stage states per cohort at checkpoint 32, and 15 graded control states per cohort (checkpoints 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 x 3 seeds).

budgets.abstention_budget: Criteria 5 and 6 bound abstention's downstream cost at checkpoint 32 (at most 36 of 144, plus 0 abstained states among the 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 states under criterion 5(d)) and on the stationary control arm (at most 32 of 240), as in the preceding protocols. Criterion 8 sets a FLOOR, not a budget, on B1 onset abstention (>= 2 of 6 states taken) - the first floor on abstention in this line, included because the selected limitation is abstention's absence at B1; it is graded jointly with criterion 8's harm conditions so that neither an always-abstaining-at-B1 profile (which would still need the harm conditions and would surface in the reported B1 successes) nor a never-abstaining profile can pass. Abstention disarmed under stable disagreement is the carried-over release mechanism, not a budget violation; abstention blocked by leg P is recorded separately (abstention_disarmed_by_purity) and is likewise not a budget violation - it is this experiment's remaining gate, and its onset cost is graded through criteria 8, 1, 3, and 4.
budgets.harm_budget: Criterion 8(b)/(c): candidate B1 pooled onset harm at most the evidence_opposition_guard baseline's B1 pooled onset harm on the SAME cohort and strictly below recent8's B1 pooled onset harm on the same cohort. Criterion 1(c): candidate B2 pooled onset harm at most the guard's B2 pooled onset harm on the same cohort and at most 60 percent of recent8's B2 pooled onset harm. Criterion 3: candidate pooled onset (all stages, checkpoints 2 and 4) harmful TEST actions at most the guard's pooled onset harm on the same cohort, with at least 5 of 6 individual onset cells at or below recent8. Criterion 4: candidate pooled return-A onset harm at most the guard's return-A onset harm on the same cohort and at most 60 percent of recent8's return-A onset harm. The restored-abstention productivity cost at B1 (each firing forfeits that state's successes) is NOT hidden by these harm budgets: B1 successes are reported in full under criterion 8, and criteria 5(b) / 6(b) bound abstention's aggregate productivity cost at checkpoint 32 and on the control arm.
budgets.train_actor_harm: No cap is claimed: the external actor's harm is a fixed cost of the shared evidence stream, identical for all methods, and is published in full per seed (criterion 7). It is never hidden inside or netted against TEST results.

expected_failure_modes: Stationary false pair passing leg P (pre-registered, the cycle's central cost-side risk): leg P is designed ARMED on stationary evidence (design purity 0.8375; realized control purity 0.784-0.968 on the higher-corroboration cohorts) and, with leg S removed, nothing else releases a stationary abstention. A stationary opposed pair therefore fires a full 16-task abstention, and a single such state at a control checkpoint where recent8 scores about 7 or more is by itself likely to fail criterion 6's successes sub-condition (margin 6) unless offset by productive control recovery elsewhere - exactly the reference-purity generation's additional-cohort failure (one state, control successes 110 vs recent8 120) and, in surviving-the-gate form, the release generation's development failure. This outcome is charged against criterion 6, not excused, and the report must state the surviving state's realized purity and acting_opposed_count.

B1 trigger sparsity (pre-registered): the abstention trigger itself fires at only about 0.45 (matched-adjusted) of B1 onset states, so a cohort drawing 0-1 triggered B1 states of 6 cannot pass criterion 8's engagement sub-condition (>= 2 taken) regardless of the gate, and its B1 harm will sit near recent8's. The records-only reference-purity-rule derivation (the ungated counterfactual, reported at every B1 state) makes sparsity-vs-gate attribution exact: if the derivation also took fewer than 2 B1 states, the failure is the trigger's sparsity; if the derivation took >= 2 and the candidate fewer, leg P blocked the difference and that is charged as a gate failure. Either way criterion 8 is charged, not excused.

Leg P disarming a B1 onset abstention on purity noise (pre-registered): the checkpoint-4 design purity is 0.8105, about 1.6 sd above the 0.70 threshold at roughly 40 matched reference events, and checkpoint-2's is 0.8375, about 2.0 sd above - so on an unlucky cohort an onset state can realize purity below 0.70 and lose a firing the ungated rule would have taken (the higher-corroboration cohorts realized 0 of 12 such B1 disarmings; the risk is small but real, it is recorded per state via abstention_disarmed_by_purity, and it is charged against criterion 8 through the lost protection).

Late abstention surviving leg P at checkpoint 32 (pre-registered, MORE likely than under either combined gate): leg P's realized checkpoint-32 arming was 3 of 9 states per cohort in the reference-purity cohorts and 6 of 9 / 4 of 9 in the abstention-release cohorts (self-fit compression raised realized purity to 0.613-0.810 against the 0.5675 global design value), so a late triggered state with realized purity at or above 0.70 (combined survival about 0.44-0.67 per triggered late state, against about 0.08-0.22 under the combined legs) still takes the abstained branch and fails criterion 5's sub-condition (d) (0 of 9 abstained states) even while sub-conditions (a)-(c) pass. That outcome would show leg P alone cannot bound the branch's late firing on realized (self-fitted) purity values, and would redirect the next cycle toward an expiry summary that is not self-fitted, under its own new protocol - the same redirect both release protocols pre-registered for this failure mode.

B1 harm restored in engagement but not in totals (pre-registered): each restored B1 abstention removes that state's recent8 harm (roughly 8-14 per state at onset) but also removes its successes; criterion 8 grades HARM (<= guard AND < recent8), not successes, at B1 - but criterion 3's pooled onset comparison and the report's full B1 successes figures keep the productivity cost visible, and a candidate that passes criterion 8's harm conditions while collapsing B1 successes toward always_abstain's 0 must be reported as such, not celebrated.

Interaction with the recovery branches at B2 and return-A (bounded, recorded, carried over): the abstention gate sits BELOW both recovery branches in the decision order, so removing leg S cannot displace a recovery firing; but at states where the graded candidates abstained because recovery was purity-disarmed, this candidate abstains MORE often than the combined-gate candidates (no support leg to fall through) - at the reference-purity generation's additional return-A checkpoint-32 state the abstention scored 0/0 against recent8's 2/14 and the ungated recovery's 13/3, so an abstention can be harm-protective and success-empty at individual late states while still failing criterion 5(d)'s records condition. Checkpoint-32 successes and harm are reported in full and any such state is named in the report.

Minority-model flip-symmetry limit (carried over, stated): the minority branch this candidate carries exploits this simulator's exact-inversion structure (original-segment flip reports reinforce the inverted class in the minority pool). The abstention gate itself is structure-agnostic (it reads only opposition against reference majorities and reference self-agreement), but any PASS remains bounded to this inversion simulator: B1 onset protection by a purity-only gated abstention branch, not a general first-contact solution, not calibrated uncertainty, and not real-world safety.

fixed_parameters.abstention_gate: CHANGED from both graded release gates by exactly ONE element: leg S (acting-window opposition support) is REMOVED entirely. The gate on the ABSTENTION branch only; the recovery branches, their authority condition, the purity gate as applied to them, the minority branch, the acting model, and every carried-over definition are unchanged. The abstention branch fires iff ALL of the following hold: (i) the carried-over trigger and arming hold (opposed_count == 2 AND abstention authority armed, i.e. NOT stable_disagreement); and (ii) LEG P - the reference-purity gate is armed (reference_purity >= 0.70, the identical quantity and threshold that bound the recovery branches, UNCHANGED). There is NO leg S: no acting-window opposed count, supporting count, or any other corroboration quantity is consulted by the gate or by any other branch. An abstention trigger whose carried-over arming holds but which leg P blocks is recorded and falls through to recent8: abstention_disarmed_by_purity is true iff leg P blocked it (purity disarmed); the flag abstention_disarmed_by_support is recorded as FALSE at every checkpoint (there is no support leg to block a state - the field is retained, with the support_threshold field recorded as null, so the record schema and the records-only derivations below stay well-defined and comparable with the graded release experiments). The acting-window opposition records are STILL COMPUTED AND RECORDED at every checkpoint exactly as in the graded release candidates (per-event records over the last 8 events: span, reference-set event count for that span, reference majority class or null, reported class, matched flag, opposed flag; acting_matched_count, acting_opposed_count, supporting_opposed_count = acting_opposed_count - opposed_count) - as RECORDS ONLY, never a decision input - so the graded higher-corroboration rule (leg P AND acting_opposed_count >= 4), the graded abstention-release rule (leg P AND acting_opposed_count >= 3), and the ungated reference-purity rule (no gate) are all derivable from this candidate's records alone and the removal's effect is attributable state by state. All gate quantities are recorded at every checkpoint: reference_purity and purity_armed (already recorded with the purity record), abstention_gate_armed (leg P alone in this experiment), abstention_disarmed_by_purity, abstention_disarmed_by_support (always false), support_threshold (null). No fitted probability, phase, stage, checkpoint, or elapsed-since-switch count enters the computation. THE SINGLE CHANGED ELEMENT OF THIS EXPERIMENT is the removal of leg S from the abstention gate; every other element of the gate, and of the candidate, is identical to the graded abstention-higher-corroboration candidate.
fixed_parameters.acting_model: A RelationOutcomeMemory (existing estimator: engineered max-minus-min span statistic, 0.25 Laplace smoothing as coded in relation_outcome_memory.py) fitted on the LAST 8 observed public events only - identically the recent8 baseline, exactly as in the graded guard, retained-recovery, joint, bounded, long-disagreement, extended-reference, minority-archive, reference-purity, abstention-release, and abstention-higher-corroboration candidates.
fixed_parameters.action_scoring: Whichever model the decision rule selects, the choice is that model's RelationOutcomeMemory.choose output. An abstention is scored as a failed task, never as a success, and is reported separately.
fixed_parameters.archive_concordance_test: IDENTICAL per-event definition to the graded candidates: for each newest-window event e, the archive expectation is the reported outcome class with the strictly highest count among ALL archive events whose span equals span(e) (tie or empty gives null); e is archive-MATCHED if its expectation is progress or damage AND e's own reported class is progress or damage; e is archive-CONCORDANT if archive-matched and its reported class EQUALS the expectation. concordant_count and archive_matched_count are in 0..2 and are recorded in full. Raw integer counts only.
fixed_parameters.authority_condition: IDENTICAL to the graded long-disagreement, extended-reference, minority-archive, reference-purity, abstention-release, and abstention-higher-corroboration candidates, unchanged and not re-tuned - all three legs, computed from the observed reported stream only, using the same span-majority machinery: (A) LOCAL-ARCHIVE DISAGREEMENT (local window = last 26 events; stable_disagreement iff comparable C >= 1 AND disagreeing D satisfies D * 2 > C); (B) ACTING-WINDOW ARCHIVE CONCORDANCE (recent_concordant_count = archive-concordant events among the last 8, in 0..8); (C) PRECEDING-WINDOW ARCHIVE DISAGREEMENT (preceding window = 26 events immediately before the local window; preceding_stable_disagreement iff C2 >= 1 AND D2 * 2 > C2; long_disagreement iff stable_disagreement AND preceding_stable_disagreement). BRANCH AUTHORITY for the carried-over branches, unchanged: ABSTENTION armed (before the abstention gate) iff NOT stable_disagreement; RECOVERY armed (before the carried-over purity gate) iff NOT stable_disagreement OR recent_concordant_count >= 2 OR long_disagreement. Would-have-fired disarmed branches are recorded (recovery_would_fire / abstention_would_fire / minority_would_fire) and fall through. The abstention gate in this experiment is an ADDITIONAL condition on the abstention branch only (see abstention_gate); it does not modify any leg of this condition, and this condition does not enter the gate's computation beyond the abstention arming it already supplied. No fitted probability, phase, stage, checkpoint, or elapsed-since-switch count enters either condition.
fixed_parameters.checkpoint: Append-only public events only; record/restore by canonical SHA256 replay exactly as the existing memory classes; restoring must reproduce the full decision record (extended-reference signal records, legacy reference-24 signal records (records-only), archive concordance records, per-event joint flags, the full authority record, the full minority record, the full purity record, AND the full abstention-gate record - per-event acting-window opposition records over the last 8 events (records-only), acting_matched_count, acting_opposed_count, supporting_opposed_count, support threshold recorded as null, abstention_gate_armed flag, abstention_disarmed_by_purity flag and abstention_disarmed_by_support flag (always false) - all counts, branch taken, acting source) and the choice identically. Maximum 1000 recorded events (existing MAX_SAMPLES).
fixed_parameters.decision_rule: Evaluated in this exact order on every decision once the signals are evaluable: (1) RECOVERY - if joint_count >= 1 AND the recovery branch is armed (carried-over authority) AND the purity gate is armed, act through the recovery model (source recorded as retained_archive), exactly as the graded candidates. (2) MINORITY RECOVERY - else if minority_joint_count >= 1 AND the minority branch is armed (minority_fraction >= 0.25 AND minority_discordant_count >= 8) AND the purity gate is armed, act through the minority model (source recorded as minority_archive), exactly as the graded candidates. (3) ABSTENTION - else if opposed_count == 2 AND the abstention branch is armed (carried-over authority) AND the abstention gate is armed (leg P: reference_purity >= 0.70; NO support leg), abstain (choose returns None). (4) RECENT8 - otherwise act through the acting model exactly. A branch whose trigger fires while the branch is disarmed - by its own arming, by the carried-over authority, by the purity gate, or (abstention only) by leg P - is recorded (recovery_would_fire / abstention_would_fire / minority_would_fire, plus recovery_disarmed_by_purity / minority_disarmed_by_purity where purity alone blocked a recovery branch, and abstention_disarmed_by_purity where leg P blocked abstention) and falls through. There is no other input: no stage, phase, rule, or switch information, no acting-window support count, and no fitted probability enters any branch.
fixed_parameters.decision_rule_rationale: Both release-gate generations priced an abstention trigger by corroboration from the six acting-window events preceding it. At checkpoint 2 those six events precede any switch that the newest pair could be announcing: under a true first switch they are previous-segment events, opposed only at the flip rate, so the bar's checkpoint-2 retention is the stationary rate by construction - the graded records confirm it exactly (every lost B1 firing in the higher-corroboration cohorts was a leg-S disarming, two of the three at acting_opposed_count exactly 2, and both additional triggers were deleted by both bars). A bar that taxes the earliest onset and the stationary false pair at the same rate, while the stationary failures it was built to stop occurred at checkpoint 8 and checkpoint 32 (where the preceding acting window is segment-internal and the bar's arithmetic differs), is not performing onset-vs-stationary separation at the checkpoint where B1 protection lives. This cycle removes that bar and keeps the one gate leg whose onset-vs-late separation is real: leg P reads the reference window's self-agreement, which is segment-pure at every onset checkpoint by design and irreducibly mixed by checkpoint 32, so it binds the abstention branch's LATE firing (the reference-purity generation's other failure site) while passing onset triggers at about 0.95. The design deliberately does NOT re-threshold any other carried-over count (the purity threshold stays at 0.70, the abstention trigger stays at opposed_count == 2, the minority arming stays at 0.25 / 8 despite its B1 non-arming being part of the limitation - changing it would confound this cycle's single-variable question), and it deliberately does NOT claim the purity-only gate identifies WHY a pair is opposed: on stationary evidence a flipped pair is locally identical to an onset pair at checkpoint 2 (pre-registered in the hypothesis), so the stationary exposure is accepted, quantified, and charged under criterion 6 - not designed away on paper.
fixed_parameters.immediate_signal: IDENTICAL to the graded extended-reference, minority-archive, reference-purity, abstention-release, and abstention-higher-corroboration candidates, unchanged and not re-tuned: for each of the newest 2 events, a hard span-majority expectation over the 50 events immediately preceding the newest window (indices N-52 .. N-3); strictly-highest reported class wins, tie or empty gives null; an event is matched if expectation and reported class are both progress or damage, and opposed if matched and different; opposed_count in 0..2; no fitted probabilities anywhere. The decision record ALSO carries the legacy reference-24 signal records (records-only, never a decision input), exactly as in the graded candidates, so the graded long candidate's rule remains derivable from the records alone.
fixed_parameters.joint_concordance_test: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: for each newest-window event e, e is JOINT if it is archive-CONCORDANT AND reference-OPPOSED (extended 50-event reference) on the SAME event. joint_count in 0..2.
fixed_parameters.minimum_events_rule: IDENTICAL to the graded extended-reference, minority-archive, reference-purity, abstention-release, and abstention-higher-corroboration candidates: the extended signal (and with it the reference purity, which reads the same 50-event reference window) requires a 2-event newest window and a full 50-event reference window (at least 52 observed events); the archive concordance test requires at least 27. Below 52 events the extended signal and the purity gate (and with it the abstention gate) are not evaluable, reference_purity is recorded as 0 with purity_armed false and the per-event purity records empty, the acting-window opposition records are empty with acting_opposed_count and supporting_opposed_count recorded as 0 and abstention_gate_armed false, joint_count and minority_joint_count are recorded as 0 (their opposed side is not evaluable), and the learner acts with a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on all available events (recorded as not evaluable, gate_evaluable false). Every benchmark checkpoint in this experiment has at least 240 observed events, so all windows are full and the fallback is never exercised during evaluation; it exists only so the class is well-defined for unit tests on short synthetic streams.
fixed_parameters.minority_archive: IDENTICAL to the graded minority-archive, reference-purity, abstention-release, and abstention-higher-corroboration candidates, unchanged and not re-tuned. Computed from the retained archive (events[:N-26]) and its own per-span majorities only. For each archive event e: let M(e) be the archive expectation for span(e) under the unchanged archive concordance definition (strictly-highest reported class among archive events of that span; tie or empty gives null). e is ARCHIVE-MATCHED if M(e) is progress or damage AND e's reported class is progress or damage. e is MINORITY (discordant) if archive-matched AND e's reported class DIFFERS from M(e). The MINORITY SET is the set of all minority archive events, in chronological order. minority_matched_count (over the archive) = number of archive-matched archive events; minority_discordant_count = size of the minority set; minority_fraction = minority_discordant_count / minority_matched_count (0 if minority_matched_count == 0). All three counts and the fraction are recorded at every checkpoint.
fixed_parameters.minority_arming: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: the minority branch is ARMED (before the carried-over purity gate) iff minority_fraction >= 0.25 AND minority_discordant_count >= 8. When the branch is not armed it cannot be taken, whatever the minority joint count says; a would-have-fired disarmed minority branch is recorded (minority_would_fire) and falls through. (At B1 onset this arming is expected NOT to hold - realized fractions 0.124-0.192 on the higher-corroboration cohorts - and that non-arming is part of this experiment's limitation evidence, not a parameter to adjust: the minority threshold is NOT changed here.)
fixed_parameters.minority_concordance_test: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: for each newest-window event e, the MINORITY EXPECTATION for span(e) is the reported outcome class with the strictly highest count among MINORITY-SET events whose span equals span(e) (tie or empty gives null). e is MINORITY-MATCHED if its minority expectation is progress or damage AND e's own reported class is progress or damage; e is MINORITY-CONCORDANT if minority-matched and its reported class EQUALS the minority expectation. minority_concordant_count and minority_matched_count (over the newest window) are in 0..2 and are recorded in full, with per-event minority records exactly as in the graded candidates.
fixed_parameters.minority_joint_test: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: for each newest-window event e, e is MINORITY-JOINT if it is MINORITY-CONCORDANT AND reference-OPPOSED (extended 50-event reference, unchanged) - both flags on the SAME event. minority_joint_count in 0..2, recorded in full with per-event minority joint flags.
fixed_parameters.minority_model: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on the MINORITY SET events only, with the existing estimator and action scoring (utility 3 * p(progress) - 10 * p(damage), deterministic action-id tie break, via RelationOutcomeMemory.choose).
fixed_parameters.recovery_model: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: a RelationOutcomeMemory fitted on the retained archive events only (events[:N-26]), with the existing estimator and action scoring (utility 3 * p(progress) - 10 * p(damage), deterministic action-id tie break, via RelationOutcomeMemory.choose).
fixed_parameters.reference_purity_gate: CARRIED OVER IDENTICALLY from the graded reference-purity candidate, unchanged and not re-tuned, and applied to the two RECOVERY branches exactly as graded there. Computed from the extended reference window (the 50 events immediately preceding the newest window, indices N-52 .. N-3 - the SAME window the immediate signal reads) and its own per-span majorities only. For each reference event e: let R(e) be the reference expectation for span(e), i.e. the reported outcome class with the strictly highest count among REFERENCE events whose span equals span(e) (tie or empty gives null). e is REFERENCE-MATCHED if R(e) is progress or damage AND e's own reported class is progress or damage; e is REFERENCE-CONCORDANT if reference-matched AND e's reported class EQUALS R(e). reference_matched_count and reference_concordant_count are over the 50 reference events; reference_purity = reference_concordant_count / reference_matched_count (0 if reference_matched_count == 0). The purity gate is ARMED iff reference_purity >= 0.70. Regular recovery fires iff joint_count >= 1 AND the carried-over recovery authority is armed AND the purity gate is armed; minority recovery fires iff minority_joint_count >= 1 AND the minority branch is armed AND the purity gate is armed (and regular recovery did not fire, per the decision order). A recovery trigger blocked by purity alone is recorded (recovery_disarmed_by_purity / minority_disarmed_by_purity) and falls through. In this experiment the same purity quantity and threshold ADDITIONALLY form the sole leg of the abstention gate (see abstention_gate), exactly the role leg P played inside both graded release gates - with leg S removed, not with any quantity re-derived or re-tuned.
fixed_parameters.retained_archive: IDENTICAL to the graded candidates: every observed event BEFORE the original reference partition, indices 0 .. N-27, i.e. events[:N-26]. Not phase-segmented, not a snapshot, and receives no phase, stage, or switch information.
fixed_parameters.threshold_justification: Fixed a priori from the simulator's known noise rates, the preceding experiments' published graded aggregates and decision records, and this simulator's published segment geometry, not from any score of this experiment (none exist). (i) SUPPORT LEG REMOVED (THE SINGLE CHANGED ELEMENT): the graded abstention-release gate introduced leg S at acting_opposed_count >= 3 and the graded higher-corroboration gate raised it to >= 4; this cycle applies NO support threshold (equivalently, the gate consults acting_opposed_count never). The removal is informed only by the preceding experiments' published records: in the higher-corroboration cohorts every leg-S disarming of an ungated B1 onset abstention (4 states) occurred at acting_opposed_count 2 or 3, three of them at exactly 2 - the value a true checkpoint-2 onset trigger realizes whenever none of its six PRE-switch acting-window predecessors is opposed, which under the own-rule opposed rate (0.1625 raw / about 0.13 adjusted) is the MODAL checkpoint-2 outcome (probability about 0.35-0.43 that a triggered checkpoint-2 state has acting_opposed_count exactly 2 given the trigger, from (1-p)^6 conditioned on the pair), not an unlucky tail. No support threshold value can fix this: any threshold >= 3 deletes the modal checkpoint-2 onset state, and a threshold of 2 is vacuous whenever the trigger holds (the pair itself contributes 2), so the leg's only non-vacuous settings are exactly the ones the two graded generations tested and both taxed B1. The choice is therefore binary - a support leg or none - and this cycle tests none, on NEW cohorts, graded on both sides. (ii) PURITY THRESHOLD 0.70: carried over UNCHANGED from the graded reference-purity protocol, as applied to the recovery branches there, to the abstention branch as leg P in both graded release protocols, and as the sole abstention-gate leg here - the identical quantity, window (50 events), and threshold. It is not re-derived and not re-tuned here. Its onset arming (design purity 0.8375 / 0.8105 at checkpoints 2 / 4, about 1.6-2.0 sd above the threshold at roughly 40 matched events; realized armed at 12 of 12 B1 onset states on the higher-corroboration cohorts) and its checkpoint-32 arming (realized 3-6 of 9 states per cohort across the two preceding generations) are the published values this cycle's criteria 8, 6, and 5 are priced against. (iii) All other carried-over thresholds are UNCHANGED and not re-tuned: newest window 2, extended reference 50, legacy reference 24, archive events[:N-26], local window 26, preceding window 26, recovery threshold joint_count >= 1, abstention trigger opposed_count == 2, strict-majority rule D * 2 > C in both authority windows, corroboration recent_concordant_count >= 2, minority fraction threshold 0.25, minority count floor 8, minority joint threshold 1, purity threshold 0.70. The only changed fixed parameter in this experiment is the abstention gate's composition: leg P alone, leg S removed.

candidate.name: AbstentionPurityOnlyRecoveryMemory
candidate.placement: New separate optional learner class in developmental_ai/. The default controller and every existing learner are untouched; existing learners appear only as baselines. The graded EvidenceOppositionGuardMemory, EvidenceOppositionRecoveryMemory, JointConcordanceRecoveryMemory, BoundedAuthorityJointRecoveryMemory, LongDisagreementJointRecoveryMemory, ExtendedReferenceJointRecoveryMemory, MinorityArchiveJointRecoveryMemory, ReferencePurityGatedRecoveryMemory, AbstentionReleaseGatedRecoveryMemory, and AbstentionHigherCorroborationRecoveryMemory are baselines in this experiment, not modified by it.

capability_under_test: First-switch (B1) onset protection without a stationary-evidence corroboration bar: whether removing the abstention release gate's support leg (leg S) entirely - so the abstention branch is gated only by reference purity (leg P, >= 0.70) on top of its carried-over trigger and authority arming - can restore B1 pooled onset harm to at or below the evidence-opposition guard's B1 harm and below recent8's B1 harm on the same cohort, with abstention actually taken at B1 onset states, without giving back stationary selectivity (criterion 6, carried form) or the checkpoint-32 release (criterion 5, including abstained branch in 0 of 9 switch-stage checkpoint-32 states) - against recent8, cumulative, frozen_A, the evidence-opposition guard, and the reference-purity, abstention-release, and abstention-higher-corroboration candidates as baselines, the higher-corroboration candidate being the decisive comparison (identical but for leg S: acting_opposed_count >= 4 there, no support leg here). Priority 1 items 2 + 3 + 4 (strengthen long-term retention; prevent new learning from overwriting established knowledge; improve adaptation to changing environments); handoff section 8 weak uncertainty calibration and excessive abstention.

checkpoints.note: A checkpoint value k means the learner has observed the full A history plus the first k TRAIN events of the named stage (control: first k continuation events). Checkpoints 2 and 4 together are the pooled onset window for criteria 8 (B1 only), 1, 2, 3, and 4; 32 grades release (criterion 5, with its abstention sub-condition) and is part of the stationary population for criterion 6; 8 and 16 report persistence costs, including the abstention gate's leg trajectory (realized purity against the design values at every checkpoint, with the acting-window opposed counts now records-only). Checkpoint values are benchmark bookkeeping only: the learner never receives k, a stage name, or any elapsed-since-switch count (see permitted_observations); the reference purity and all windows are fixed observed-stream summaries, not segment measurements - the design values by checkpoint are consequences of the published segment geometry acting on those summaries, not inputs to the learner. Checkpoint 0 is a reported diagnostic, NOT graded: at k=0 the stream contains zero post-switch events, so no evidence-driven learner can distinguish the switched world from the pre-switch world.

expected_failure_modes: Stationary false pair passing leg P (pre-registered, the cycle's central cost-side risk): leg P is designed ARMED on stationary evidence (design purity 0.8375; realized control purity 0.784-0.968 on the higher-corroboration cohorts) and, with leg S removed, does not release stationary abstention at all. A stationary opposed pair therefore fires a full 16-task abstention, and a single such state at a control checkpoint where recent8 scores about 7 or more is by itself likely to fail criterion 6's successes sub-condition (margin 6) unless offset by productive control recovery elsewhere, exactly as the reference-purity generation's additional cohort failed (one state, -10 successes gross) and the release generation's development cohort failed in surviving-gate form. This outcome is charged against criterion 6, not excused, and the report must state the surviving state's realized purity and acting_opposed_count. A no-trigger criterion-6 PASS must be reported as a no-trigger PASS, as in the preceding grading.

B1 trigger sparsity (pre-registered): the gate can only restore firings the trigger produces; at the design per-state trigger probability of about 0.45 (matched-adjusted) a cohort can draw 0-1 triggered B1 onset states of 6, failing criterion 8(a) on sparsity and leaving B1 harm near recent8's, failing 8(c). The records-only reference-purity-rule derivation distinguishes sparsity (derivation also < 2 taken) from gate blockage (derivation >= 2 taken, candidate fewer, each difference a leg-P disarming) - the attribution is reported either way and the criterion is charged either way.

B1 harm not restored despite restored engagement (pre-registered): restored abstentions remove harm only at the states where they fire; if the triggered states are the low-harm draws (recent8 harm per B1 onset state varies widely) or if untriggered B1 states carry the cohort's harm, criterion 8(b) or 8(c) can fail with 8(a) passing. The per-state harm decomposition (candidate vs guard vs recent8 at each of the 6 B1 onset states, with the branch taken at each) is reported so this is distinguishable from engagement failure.

Late abstention surviving leg P at checkpoint 32 (pre-registered, more likely than under either combined gate): leg P's realized checkpoint-32 arming was 3 of 9 states per cohort in the reference-purity cohorts and 6 of 9 / 4 of 9 in the abstention-release cohorts (self-fit compression raised realized purity to 0.613-0.810 against the 0.5675 global design value), so a late state with purity at or above 0.70 still takes the abstained branch and fails criterion 5's sub-condition (d) (0 of 9 abstained states) even while sub-conditions (a)-(c) pass. That outcome would show leg P alone cannot bound the branch's late firing on realized (self-fitted) purity values, and would redirect the next cycle toward an expiry summary that is not self-fitted, under its own new protocol.

Leg P disarming onset abstention on purity noise (pre-registered, carried over): the checkpoint-4 design purity is 0.8105, about 1.6 sd above the 0.70 threshold at roughly 40 matched reference events (checkpoint 2: 0.8375, about 2.0 sd), so on an unlucky cohort an onset state - at B1 (charged under criterion 8) or at B2 / return-A (charged under criteria 1, 3, and 4) - can realize purity below 0.70 and lose a firing the ungated rule would have taken; any realized onset purity disarming is recorded and charged through the lost protection.

Criterion 4 failing again on the carried profile, independent of the gate (pre-registered, carried over): the graded abstention-higher-corroboration candidate FAILed criterion 4 on additional while being identical to its decisive baselines at return-A onset; the return-A harm ceiling and guard comparison are cohort-relative, so the same carried profile can miss them on a new cohort regardless of the abstention gate's composition. Such a failure is charged unchanged and reported as inherited, exactly as in the preceding gradings - it neither vindicates nor condemns the removed leg, and the records-only derivations make the attribution checkable.

Interaction with the recovery branches at B2 and return-A (bounded, recorded, carried over): the abstention gate sits BELOW both recovery branches in the decision order, so it cannot displace a recovery firing; but at states where the graded candidates fell through a gate-blocked abstention to recent8, this candidate abstains instead - the abstention can ADD success loss at individual states (0 successes against recent8's positive line) while removing harm, and at late states it is charged under criterion 5(d) regardless of its harm benefit. Checkpoint-32 successes and harm are reported in full and any such state is named in the report.

Minority-model flip-symmetry limit (carried over, stated): the minority branch this candidate carries exploits this simulator's exact-inversion structure (original-segment flip reports reinforce the inverted class in the minority pool). The abstention gate itself is structure-agnostic (it reads only opposition counts against reference majorities and reference self-agreement), but any PASS remains bounded to this inversion simulator: first-switch protection by a purity-only gated abstention branch, not a general first-contact or excessive-abstention solution, not calibrated uncertainty, and not real-world safety.

hypothesis: The graded higher-corroboration records localize the B1 failure to leg S's structure, not to the abstention branch or to leg P: (i) at B1 onset the minority branch was unarmed at every state on both cohorts (fractions 0.124-0.192) and regular recovery took 0 of 6 B1 onset states on additional and at most 1 of 6 on development-type cohorts throughout this line, so abstention is the only branch that can move B1 harm; (ii) the ungated reference-purity rule, derivable from the candidate's own records, would have abstained at 4 of 6 pooled B1 onset states on development and 2 of 6 on additional in the higher-corroboration cohorts, and the candidate took only 2 of those 6 - every lost firing was blocked by leg S alone (abstention_disarmed_by_support true, abstention_disarmed_by_purity false), three of them at acting_opposed_count exactly 2 (all checkpoint 2, supporting_opposed_count 0) and one at acting_opposed_count 3 (checkpoint 4, seed 412039, the single graded outcome the >= 4 raise changed anywhere); (iii) leg P blocked NO B1 onset abstention on either cohort (realized B1 onset purity 0.757-0.964, armed at 12 of 12 states), consistent with its design arming at onset (0.8375 / 0.8105 against the 0.70 threshold, about 0.95 armed probability). Removing leg S while keeping leg P therefore restores, by construction, every B1 onset abstention that leg P allows - retention against the ungated rule rises from the >= 4 bar's realized 2 of 6 (design pooled leg-S retention about 0.41-0.55) to leg P's onset arming rate of about 0.95 - and the B1 harm consequence is graded directly as PRIMARY criterion 8: on the higher-corroboration cohorts the lost B1 firings cost +16 pooled onset harm for one development firing and left additional's B1 harm at recent8's 88 against the guard's 58, while the ungated (reference-purity) generation's B1 harm was 31 / 58 on its own cohorts. The cost side is pre-computed with the same rates and is the reason this is a hypothesis rather than a revert: on stationary evidence a triggered pair (opposed_count == 2, per-state probability about 0.017 matched-adjusted / 0.026 raw) now survives whenever leg P is armed, and leg P is designed ARMED on stationary evidence (design purity 0.8375; realized control purity 0.784-0.968 on the higher-corroboration cohorts, armed at every graded control checkpoint recorded there) - so this candidate's stationary behavior is, by design, the ungated branch's: an expected roughly 0.25-0.40 triggered stationary states per cohort, each a full 16-task abstention costing up to about 7 successes against criterion 6's margin of 6, exactly the failure the reference-purity generation realized once on additional (control checkpoint 32, seed 383017, purity 0.886) and the release generation realized once on development (control checkpoint 8, seed 392039). Criterion 6 is therefore a genuine co-graded guard, not a formality: this cycle bets that B1 onset protection - a systematic effect, expected at roughly 2.5 of 6 states per cohort - is worth re-exposing the stationary lottery that the corroboration legs were built, and on the records failed, to close at checkpoint 2. The checkpoint-32 side is intermediate by design: leg P alone was armed at 3 of 9 checkpoint-32 states per cohort in the reference-purity cohorts (realized purity 0.645-0.810) and at 6 of 9 / 4 of 9 in the abstention-release cohorts, so a triggered late state survives with probability roughly 0.44-0.67 under leg P alone, against roughly 0.08-0.22 under the combined legs; criterion 5(d) (0 of 9 abstained states) is carried unchanged so any late regression is charged, not excused. The limitation this cycle selects is the one that grading named and that the preceding cycle's own records localize exactly: first-switch (B1) onset non-protection in the gated family. At B1 neither recovery branch can protect - regular recovery is archive-blocked (a B1-following event is archive-discordant by construction) and the minority branch was unarmed at every B1 onset state on both graded higher-corroboration cohorts (realized minority fractions 0.124-0.192, against its 0.25 arming threshold) - so abstention is the family's only protective response at B1, and the two release-gate generations have thinned it to 32 of 96 B1 onset episode-checkpoints abstained on development and 0 of 96 on additional. The state-level records show WHY, and it is a structural defect in the gate, not a draw: every B1 checkpoint-2 trigger the ungated (reference-purity) rule would have taken on the higher-corroboration cohorts - 1 of 3 development states and 2 of 3 additional states - was blocked by the release gate's leg S ALONE at acting_opposed_count exactly 2 (the triggering pair itself, supporting_opposed_count 0), and both release-gate generations (>= 3 and >= 4) blocked both additional triggers. At checkpoint 2 the six acting-window events preceding the triggering pair are, under a true switch, PRE-switch events: they are previous-segment evidence, opposed only at the own-rule flip rate, so a corroboration bar priced on them systematically deletes exactly the earliest onset protection while a stationary false pair - whose preceding events have the identical distribution - is priced identically. Leg S therefore cannot do the job it was built for at checkpoint 2: it does not separate onset from stationary there, it merely taxes both, and the onset side of the tax is what failed criteria 3 and 4. This cycle changes exactly one thing: it REMOVES leg S from the abstention release gate entirely. The abstention branch fires iff the carried-over trigger and arming hold (opposed_count == 2 AND NOT stable_disagreement) AND leg P holds (reference_purity >= 0.70, the identical frozen quantity and threshold that already bound both recovery branches and formed leg P of both release gates). Leg P is not a corroboration bar on the trigger: it is a segment-purity condition on the reference window that is armed by design at every onset checkpoint (design purity 0.8375 at checkpoint 2, 0.8105 at checkpoint 4; realized armed at 12 of 12 B1 onset states on the higher-corroboration cohorts) and disarmed at roughly half of checkpoint-32 states - it separates onset from LATE, which is the separation the checkpoint-32 release (criterion 5, including sub-condition (d)) actually used, while leg S's claimed onset-vs-stationary separation is the one the records show does not exist at checkpoint 2. This cycle's headline criterion is therefore a NEW criterion 8, B1 onset protection, graded as PRIMARY; criteria 6 (stationary selectivity) and 5 (checkpoint-32 release including (d)) are the co-graded guards the removal must not give back, and criteria 1, 4, 2, 3 are carried in identical form.
